reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the pair, separately reread the 2026–27 Chemistry regulations and official thesis entry guidance, and reconstructed the required core, elective levels and profiling balance from the underlying sources. Reconsidered the university course descriptions against the selected UCR course evidence, including the five separated rows and the distinct outcomes of the two UCR plans. Checked that the reader-facing titles, study explanations and caution reflect the evidence. Worker B conducted both passes.
findings: The 2026–27 regulations specify 135 EC in the major plus 45 EC of profiling. The major includes eight 7.5 EC first-year courses, 7.5 EC of required biochemical methods and academic skills and a 15 EC chemistry thesis (82.5 EC). The selected 52.5 EC of major electives comprises 37.5 EC at level 2 and 15 EC at level 3. The example takes molecular modelling and structure determination in category 1, Biochemistry 2 in category 2, and Physical Chemistry 2 and Inorganic and Solid-State Chemistry in category 3. Solids and Surfaces and Advanced Physical Chemistry are level-3 major electives. Molecules and Materials is an illustrative direction; it is not a named requirement or distinct degree. The earlier Molecular Life Sciences track is discontinued and is not the Molecules and Life interest direction.

Table 1.1 requires at least 45 EC at level 3 across the whole degree. The major contributes 30 EC at level 3 including the thesis, leaving at least 15 EC of level-3 profiling in this example. This also meets the profiling requirement of at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3. The two generic profiling slots total 45 EC and are not assigned fictitious courses. The thesis requires 120 earned EC and commonly takes place in the final period, with timing arranged with a research group. The example places foundational chemistry and mathematical and experimental methods before the advanced materials and physical chemistry courses. Physical Chemistry 2 precedes Advanced Physical Chemistry. Article 3.3 establishes Dutch as predominant at level 1, both Dutch and English at level 2, and English at level 3.

The closest plan pairs laboratory and biomolecular foundations with environmental biogeochemistry, materials cycles and energy. Soils & Aquifers contributes field and laboratory analysis, and Earth System Science Tools contributes tracer and proxy methods. Resource courses supply recycling, remediation and aqueous and mineral geochemistry. Linear Systems replaces the stakeholder project formerly scheduled in 2028h2: that project is offered only in the first planning term. The replacement builds from Mathematical Methods and introductory data analysis to model linear system responses, without an implied spectroscopy equivalence. Product Design supplies a late applied project on design, prototyping and resource choices. The other plan develops biomolecular understanding through cell biology, pathology, anatomy, physiology, immunology and pharmacology, with experimental methods, epidemiology and evidence synthesis. The brain and neurobiology courses supply a bounded neural case context and support the research progression. Neither plan promises drug synthesis or experimental medicinal chemistry. The 13 unique courses per side distinguish the academic outcomes. Introductory spectroscopy, crystallography, microscopy and chemical testing in Sustainability Essentials II and inorganic lab work in R3 are relevant to specialist chemistry, but do not form a sustained synthesis, structural analysis, thermodynamics and advanced lab sequence. Three rows have focused overlap: calculus, biochemical function and life science experimentation. The other five former rows shared tools or topics but omitted a central disciplinary aim or lab sequence and are now separate. Both UCR choices remain related directions under the caution presentation.
